title: Roman school distinguishes living and dead faith as we do
source_text: XLI. Primum igitur sciendum est Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae fidem, ut & nos, distinguere in vivam & mortuam, & distinctionem illam eodem modo exponere. Nam per fidem mortuam intelligunt assensum otiosum & inertem qui verbo Dei adhibetur: quemque nec Dei dilectio, nec ulla vere bona opera comitantur. Et per fidem vivam illam quae activa est, & operans per dilectionem, quaeque & Dei amorem, & fiduciam in eum includit. Et prioris etiam actum per credere Deo, posterioris per credere in Deum, significare solent. Quae distinctio apud eos ita recepta atque vulgaris est, ut superfluum sit eorum hac de re hic referre testimonia.
pass_a_gloss: First, therefore, it must be known that the Doctors of the Roman Church distinguish faith, as we also do, into living and dead, and explain that distinction in the same way. For by dead faith they understand an idle and inert assent given to the Word of God, which neither the love of God nor any truly good works accompany. And by living faith that which is active and working through love, and which includes both love of God and trust in him. And they are accustomed to signify the act of the former by believing God, of the latter by believing in God. Which distinction is so received and common among them that it is superfluous to report their testimonies on this matter here.
pass_b_english: Romans distinguish living vs dead faith as we do: idle assent vs faith working through love.
Dead faith: believe God; living: believe in God—with love and trust.

lemmas.gloss: to distinguish faith into living and dead
to believe God ... to believe in God

choices.why: Roman dead faith = bare assent without love/works.
